surface_verification.runner: the bootstrapper-checks job's exact four-step sequence, executed against a CLEAN tree staged outside the worktree
surface_verification.justification: This diff has no web surface: it changes .github/workflows/ci.yml, adds tests under bootstrapper/test/ and scripts/ci/tests/, and edits two server test COMMENTS. No API route, store mutation, SSE/WS handler, message contract, or UI-consumed code is touched, so the Backend-affects-Frontend rule does not force surface=web. The honest end-to-end for a CI-job change is the job itself, so the four steps ran against a clean copy of bootstrapper/: npm ci (from the lockfile alone, no node_modules present) -> npx tsc --noEmit -> npm run lint -> npm test. THAT RUN FOUND A REAL CONSTRAINT: the first clean-tree attempt FAILED 1/196 because test/guards.test.mjs asserts version parity by reading ../server/package.json, which a bootstrapper-only tree lacks. With the sibling package.json present - which actions/checkout@v4 always provides - all four steps exit 0 and every test passes. That constraint is now documented in the workflow and ratcheted by test_the_job_checks_out_the_WHOLE_repo, so a future sparse-checkout optimisation fails loudly instead of confusingly. The live contract test really did reach the network in this run (HTTP 200, 14 plugins, parsed, marketplace id and all sources verified). Three further real executions back the count: ctx.skip verified to keep the suite green against an unresolvable host; the ::warning annotation verified emitted under GITHUB_ACTIONS=true; and the schedule-mandatory branch verified BOTH to throw under GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=schedule with an unreachable host AND not to false-red under the same env with a healthy network. Playwright E2E is skipped by design - there is no browser-visible behaviour in this diff - and the ubuntu-latest/Node-20 arm of the job is confirmed by this PR's own first CI run, which is stated in the handoff rather than claimed here.
